prior_summary: Fresh-current-TCP Cartesian increments provide local feedback at perturbed intermediate states, while a registered four-class causal phase head regularizes carry, opening/settling, deposited-retreat and handle-ready separation.
applicable_conditions: Prefer when block and destination remain in the demonstrated corridor but TCP/object height, lag or release timing is unusual and two causal frames provide consistent motion evidence. It is useful in the 900:1160 release-to-closing overlap.
termination_guidance: Transfer to close_drawer only after observed floor-height stationarity and detachment, not from the learned phase class alone. Prefer a late transfer when TCP is at the handle; preserve both causal history frames across the switch.
limitations: Local increments can drift and are not invariant to large object or drawer displacement. Coarse phase labels are action/geometry supervision, not contact truth. Two frames may not resolve noisy settling; unseen slip/drop recovery, collision avoidance and IK feasibility are not established.
